A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a theoretical framework for Hawkes processes, which allows us to understand the effect of different priors on the generalization error of our model.
we have provided a theoretical justification for a data-driven approach to the problem of unveiling social network structure from user interactions.
we have a new way to understand the Hawkes process as a multivariate time series and we have a new data-driven approach to estimate the Hawkes process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of Hawkes processes, the use of data-driven penalizations is crucial to achieve good generalization performances.
the use of data-driven penalties is crucial for the estimation of sparse or low-rank networks, and that the generalization error bound can be used to construct such penalties.
a simple and natural model for high-frequency user interactions in a dynamic network can be used to recover its latent network structure with provable guarantees.
